summary:
Región de Murcia stands under Spain's national framework. The region's own layer is Ley 8/2016 of 27 May 2016 (BOE-A-2016-6170), which prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, and sex characteristics across public and private activity in the region. Within its scope the statute bars any requirement that a person prove a declared gender identity by psychological or medical report, so a regional service, clinic or venue cannot demand documentation of a visitor's gender as a condition of service.

Article 5 creates the Observatorio regional contra la discriminación por orientación sexual e identidad de género, a participation and consultation body on which LGTBI entities are represented.

Title IV sets the sanctioning ladder. Minor breaches draw a warning or a fine of up to EUR 3,000. Serious breaches run EUR 3,001 to EUR 20,000 and cover degrading remarks or incitement to violence against LGBTI people or their families in the provision of services. Very serious breaches run EUR 20,001 to EUR 45,000, with accessory penalties that include exclusion from regional public aid for up to one year. Multiple discrimination raises the grade of the infraction.

Murcia was among eight autonomous regions that approved LGBTI and trans equality laws in the 2010s, and Ley 8/2016 remains the operative regional instrument. Implementation of the national trans-equality law falls to the regional government.
tangentialFactors:
The regional statute's remedies are administrative rather than criminal, so a refusal of service or a degrading remark in Murcia runs through the regional sanctioning regime and the observatory rather than a prosecution.

The protected grounds include sex characteristics alongside gender identity and expression, and the serious-breach tier names the families of LGBTI people, which reaches a trans visitor travelling with a partner or relatives.

The statute's scope is public and private activity in the region, which covers service providers, employers, healthcare and housing within Murcia rather than only regional public bodies.
localsOnly:
For residents, Ley 8/2016 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, and sex characteristics in employment, healthcare, housing, education and the provision of services in the region, and bars any demand that a person prove a declared gender identity by psychological or medical report.

The Observatorio regional contra la discriminación por orientación sexual e identidad de género is the regional consultation body for these questions, with LGTBI entities represented on it.

Breaches are graded and sanctioned by the regional administration: a warning or up to EUR 3,000 for minor breaches, EUR 3,001 to EUR 20,000 for serious breaches, and EUR 20,001 to EUR 45,000 for very serious breaches, with exclusion from regional public aid for up to one year available as an accessory penalty. Multiple discrimination raises the grade.

Implementation of the national trans-equality law falls to the regional government, so the regional administration is the body that carries the national statute into practice in Murcia.
outOfScopeNotes:
No region-specific enforcement action, prosecution or incident of anti-trans violence in Murcia appears in the sources, and the practical operation of the regional statute's sanctioning regime is not documented.

Attitude survey data is not disaggregated to Murcia; the available figures date from 2013 and 2016.

The sources do not describe how Ley 8/2016 and the 2023 national statute interact in practice, whether the observatory is currently active, or whether the region issues guidance on facilities, healthcare or schools.
